actions.justification: Mandatory first step per AHA guidelines. Continuous vital sign monitoring (HR, BP, SpO2, RR) is required immediately at presentation for all acute chest pain patients.
Mandatory per AHA Class I guidelines: 12-lead ECG must be obtained and interpreted within 10 minutes of first medical contact to confirm STEMI and guide emergent reperfusion therapy.
Mandatory immediate history and physical for risk stratification. Important to characterize onset (18 hours), quality, associated symptoms, and confirm STEMI diagnosis prior to treatment decisions.

MANDATORY: Immediate cath lab activation is required for primary PCI. Door-to-balloon target is <90 minutes and patient is already 15 minutes post-arrival with confirmed STEMI and ongoing symptoms at 18 hours onset.
MANDATORY: Aspirin 325mg chewable is Class I recommendation for STEMI as part of dual antiplatelet therapy. Must be given immediately unless contraindicated.
MANDATORY: P2Y12 inhibitor (ticagrelor or clopidogrel) is required as part of dual antiplatelet therapy for STEMI per AHA guidelines. Administer as loading dose prior to PCI.
MANDATORY: Heparin or enoxaparin is required as adjunctive anticoagulation for STEMI per AHA guidelines. This is the only remaining mandatory action and must be completed immediately.
Primary PCI is the preferred reperfusion strategy for STEMI. Door-to-balloon target is <90 minutes. Patient has been in ED 30 minutes so PCI must be arranged urgently to meet the time target.
IV access is essential for administering anticoagulation and other IV medications. Must be established to facilitate heparin administration and ongoing STEMI management.
SpO2 is 95%, which is borderline. Supplemental oxygen is indicated to maintain SpO2 ≥95% per guidelines, especially in the setting of active STEMI with ongoing ischemia.
High-sensitivity troponin should be obtained at presentation to confirm myocardial injury, establish a baseline, and support diagnosis per AHA guidelines (Class I).

Right-sided ECG (V4R) is indicated to rule out right ventricular infarction, particularly important before considering nitrates for ongoing chest pain. This is critical for safety per AHA guidelines on inferior STEMI.
Cardiology consultation is essential to coordinate primary PCI, review ECG findings including right-sided leads, and guide ongoing management of this STEMI patient with 18 hours of symptoms.

Patient is hemodynamically stable (BP 148/90, HR 88, no signs of cardiogenic shock or pulmonary edema). Beta-blocker is indicated per AHA guidelines as adjunctive therapy in STEMI to reduce myocardial oxygen demand, especially given hypertension and tachycardia-prone diabetic patient.

Patient has ongoing chest discomfort 18 hours after symptom onset. Morphine can provide analgesia and reduce sympathetic activation in the setting of ongoing ischemic pain, though should be used judiciously.

Formal ECG interpretation is needed to document STEMI territory, assess for RV involvement from the right-sided ECG already obtained, and guide further management decisions including nitrate use and PCI planning.

Patient has ongoing chest pain with hypertension (BP 148/90). Right-sided ECG (V4R) was already obtained to rule out RV infarction. If no RV involvement is confirmed, nitrates are indicated for symptom relief and BP management per AHA guidelines.

Patient has had chest pain onset 18 hours ago with persistent ST elevation. At 85 minutes since arrival, the door-to-balloon target of <90 minutes is at risk. If PCI cannot be completed within the recommended timeframe, fibrinolysis should be considered per AHA guidelines as a rescue reperfusion strategy.

Obtaining prior ECG for comparison can help characterize the extent and evolution of ST changes, differentiate new from old changes, and assist in risk stratification for this STEMI patient with hypertension and diabetes.

Patient has SpO2 of 95% and BP 148/90 with ongoing STEMI. All mandatory STEMI actions are completed. Cautious IV fluid support may help maintain perfusion. Avoid aggressive fluid loading given hypertension, but gentle crystalloid is appropriate supportive care while awaiting PCI.

Patient has SpO2 of 95% and BP 148/90 with ongoing STEMI. All mandatory STEMI actions are completed. This optional crystalloid bolus can support hemodynamic stability while awaiting PCI, especially given the patient's presentation with ongoing ischemia. Careful fluid administration is warranted given hypertension and diabetes comorbidities.

Patient has confirmed STEMI with markedly elevated troponin, persistent ST elevation at 18 hours, and ongoing discomfort. Cath lab has been activated and PCI arranged. Admission to CCU is indicated for continuous cardiac monitoring, hemodynamic surveillance, and post-PCI care.
Risk stratification (e.g., TIMI or GRACE score) is appropriate for this STEMI patient with hypertension and diabetes to guide intensity of adjunctive therapy and post-PCI management planning.

Given the 18-hour symptom onset with persistent chest pain and ST elevation, formal assessment for early invasive strategy timing and appropriateness supports guideline-directed care and informs the interventional team.
